syllabus.summary: Project-based Python course covering web services, persistence, testing, and readable engineering documentation.

sections.heading: Course Description
sections.body: Students build maintainable Python applications with web routes, relational data models, templates, and clear verification steps. The final project emphasizes practical design decisions and defensible tradeoffs.

sections.heading: Major Assignments
sections.body: Weekly labs, two code reviews, one data-layer checkpoint, one interface checkpoint, and a final deployed demo with tests and setup documentation.

sections.heading: Grading Policy
sections.body: Labs 30%, checkpoints 20%, final project 35%, participation and code review 15%. Late work uses the course grace-token policy documented in class.

sections.heading: Technology Expectations
sections.body: Students should use Python 3.12, virtual environments, Git, SQLite, and server-rendered templates unless an assignment explicitly authorizes another stack.

materials.title: Python Crash Course
materials.note: Used for early syntax and testing review.

materials.title: Fluent Python
materials.note: Recommended for students who want deeper Python idioms.

syllabus.summary: Foundational programming course focused on algorithms, debugging, functions, collections, files, and programming habits.

sections.heading: Learning Outcomes
sections.body: Students will design small programs, trace control flow, use core data structures, write functions, and explain test cases in plain language.

sections.heading: Lab Policy
sections.body: Labs are completed during scheduled sessions. Students may revise lab submissions within one week after feedback.

sections.heading: Academic Integrity
sections.body: Students may discuss concepts, but submitted code must reflect individual work unless collaboration is explicitly assigned.

materials.title: Python Crash Course
materials.note: Same required text as CPS 3320, reused across the programming sequence.

syllabus.summary: Professional communication course covering memos, reports, proposals, revision workflows, and audience analysis.

sections.heading: Writing Portfolio
sections.body: Students maintain a portfolio of drafts and revisions for workplace documents, including a final reflection on audience and tone decisions.

sections.heading: Attendance
sections.body: Workshops depend on peer review. Students should notify the instructor before missing a workshop day.

materials.title: Technical Communication Today
materials.note: Any legal rental, used, or library copy is acceptable.

syllabus.summary: Discrete mathematics course for computing students, including proofs, sets, relations, counting, graphs, and recurrence relations.

sections.heading: Assessment
sections.body: Problem sets 35%, quizzes 15%, midterm 20%, final exam 25%, participation 5%. Students must show reasoning, not only final answers.

sections.heading: Calculator and Software Policy
sections.body: Symbolic tools may be used for exploration after manual solutions are attempted. Exams are closed-book unless announced otherwise.

materials.title: Discrete Mathematics and Its Applications
materials.note: Earlier editions may differ in exercise numbering.

syllabus.summary: Operations course covering process design, capacity, inventory, quality, forecasting, and supply chain tradeoffs.

sections.heading: Case Discussions
sections.body: Students prepare short decision memos before case days. Case work emphasizes operational evidence and clear recommendations.

sections.heading: Team Project
sections.body: Teams analyze a service or production process and propose measurable improvements using course concepts.

materials.title: Operations Management
materials.note: Used for weekly problem sets and case background.

syllabus.summary: Speech course focused on audience analysis, structure, delivery, evidence, and constructive peer feedback.

sections.heading: Speech Sequence
sections.body: Students deliver introductory, informative, persuasive, and special occasion speeches with outlines and reflection notes.

sections.heading: Recording Policy
sections.body: Presentations may be recorded for self-review and grading. Recordings remain within the course environment.

syllabus.summary: Comparative literature course reading global short fiction, drama, and poetry with attention to translation, historical context, and close reading.

sections.heading: Reading Journal
sections.body: Students submit short reading notes before discussion days. Notes should quote one passage and ask one interpretive question.

sections.heading: Essay Sequence
sections.body: Two analytical essays build from passage analysis to comparative argument. Revision memos are required with final drafts.

sections.heading: Discussion Expectations
sections.body: Class sessions depend on prepared conversation. Students should bring the assigned text and annotate passages for discussion.

materials.title: The Norton Anthology of World Literature
materials.note: Selected volumes are used across the semester.

syllabus.summary: Precalculus course reviewing functions, trigonometry, exponential models, logarithms, and algebraic techniques for later calculus coursework.

sections.heading: Homework
sections.body: Problem practice is assigned weekly. Students should show intermediate work and review feedback before quizzes.

sections.heading: Quiz Policy
sections.body: Short quizzes check recent skills and may include algebraic simplification, graph interpretation, and trigonometric identities.

sections.heading: Placement Support
sections.body: Students who need additional review should attend office hours or math tutoring during the first three weeks.

materials.title: Precalculus: Mathematics for Calculus
materials.authors: James Stewart, Lothar Redlin, Saleem Watson
materials.note: Useful as a supplemental reference for practice problems.
